bug_semantics: OliveTin authorizes action execution and log disclosure independently. A caller granted exec:true but logs:false could invoke StartActionAndWait or StartActionByGetAndWait; each handler waited for the execution, fetched its InternalLogEntry, converted it to the public LogEntry (including stdout/stderr/output and exit status), and returned it without applying IsAllowedLogs. The synchronous response therefore disclosed exactly the output that GetLogs and the other log-bearing paths were meant to withhold.
flaw_origin: The synchronous wait endpoints already existed when log visibility was not an independent ACL permission. The causal flaw began when PR #273's sole member commit 2338cd0cc8e1fe2a9729c58bf31fbfc5dc342feb introduced PermissionsList.Logs and IsAllowedLogs, and guarded GetLogs, but left both pre-existing synchronous response paths returning internalLogEntryToPb(...) unguarded. This created the exec:true/logs:false policy state while omitting enforcement on the two immediate-output paths. The member was squash-landed as db5de9be9793be65e2a77ab71656713f97bc779b; later refactors and file moves preserved the omission until the 2026 fix.
ai_marker: absent on the BIC commit object: `git cat-file -p 2338cd0cc8e1fe2a9729c58bf31fbfc5dc342feb` shows human author and committer `jamesread <contact@jread.com>` and the message `feature: #135 Permissions for logs`; there are no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot, or other AI attribution trailers.
evidence: Advisory: https://github.com/OliveTin/OliveTin/security/advisories/GHSA-jm28-2wcr-qf3h identifies StartActionAndWait and StartActionByGetAndWait, affected Go versions `< 0.0.0-20260708085316-e421780c9885`, and fix e421780c9885aa5024d2f47b4ed4898f2f18eb90. Policy origin: issue https://github.com/OliveTin/OliveTin/issues/135 explicitly requested a new `logs` ACL independent of view/exec, including exec:true/logs:false configurations. `git log --all -S 'Logs bool' -- service/internal/config/config.go internal/config/config.go` identifies squash landing db5de9be9793be65e2a77ab71656713f97bc779b (`feature: #135 Permissions for logs (#273)`). GitHub PR https://github.com/OliveTin/OliveTin/pull/273/commits lists exactly one member, 2338cd0cc8e1fe2a9729c58bf31fbfc5dc342feb; stable `git patch-id` for that member and db5de9be9793be65e2a77ab71656713f97bc779b is identically 9df6cd02b8c7f15c47318a7f9148fbb6ebdcaa15, proving the squash decomposition. `git show 2338cd0...` adds `Logs bool` in internal/config/config.go, `IsAllowedLogs` in internal/acl/acl.go, and an IsAllowedLogs guard only in GetLogs at internal/grpcapi/grpcApi.go:237. In that same BIC tree, `git grep` shows StartActionAndWait at internal/grpcapi/grpcApi.go:58 returning `LogEntry: internalLogEntryToPb(internalLogEntry)` at line 76 and StartActionByGetAndWait at line 101 doing the same at line 119, with no logs check. Immediate-parent verification: `git show 5f3a96751509cfd0a93ac417577023218f2ece0c:internal/config/config.go` shows PermissionsList containing only View and Exec, and `git grep -e IsAllowedLogs -e Permissions.Logs 5f3a967... -- internal` returns no matches. The parent does contain both synchronous return paths, but the independently denyable Logs permission and thus the advisory's exec:true/logs:false bypass do not yet exist; this directly establishes parent absence of the flawed policy/enforcement combination. History: `git log -L` traces the wait endpoints back through later moves to their 2023 introduction, confirming that the 2024 permission commit, not a later move/refactor, is the smallest causal BIC. Version boundary: squash landing db5de9be9793be65e2a77ab71656713f97bc779b is contained first by tag 2024.04.18 (tag commit 4c2cc5da1c6f6c0d3f9db71d8f2173104bc80ba6); its parent describes to 2024.04.14, placing the practical vulnerable-release boundary at 2024.04.18 within the advisory's coarse `< patched pseudoversion` range. Fix: direct commit 904616b1b1ef995ab868431b0835cb3fc368be7b adds logEntryForAllowedViewer/requireLogEntryAllowed and makes both synchronous handlers obtain their response only after the logs ACL check. Merge e421780c9885aa5024d2f47b4ed4898f2f18eb90 has parents 995ff79736f2bccc364448a3ece84087b550b232 and 904616b1b1ef995ab868431b0835cb3fc368be7b. `git tag --contains e421780c... --sort=creatordate` begins with 3000.17.0, whose peeled commit is d0075a7a8d44028793ea3384b34062b940841f24, matching the advisory's first patched release. The Cursor co-author trailer is on the 2026 direct fix only and is excluded by the BIC-only attribution rule.
reasoning: The endpoint code alone predates the security boundary, so treating its 2023 introduction or its 2025 Connect migration as the BIC would confuse a previously unrestricted output API with the later authorization bypass. The exploit becomes possible only when the product promises an independently false `logs` permission while still allowing `exec`. The sole PR #273 member is therefore the smallest causal commit: it creates that permission, implements its checker, and demonstrates intended enforcement on GetLogs, yet omits both synchronous log-returning handlers already present in its tree. Its immediate parent has the same handlers but no Logs field/checker, so the exact advisory state is absent. The squash was decomposed to the original one-member commit and patch identity was verified; db5de9be9793be65e2a77ab71656713f97bc779b is only the mainline landing. Later history preserves the same unguarded returns until direct fix 904616b1b1ef995ab868431b0835cb3fc368be7b, merged as advisory/pseudoversion commit e421780c9885aa5024d2f47b4ed4898f2f18eb90 and released in 3000.17.0. Finally, only the BIC commit object was used for AI attribution: it is authored and committed by jamesread and has no AI marker, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI notwithstanding Cursor attribution on the fix.
